cues.en: Language, in many respects, is a vital part of the human experience, and language is interlinked with cognitive development in many important ways. When children have structured language, it helps them make sense of the world. And this is true whether the kids are communicating verbally or whether they're using signs and gestures. When deaf people have strokes, it affects their ability to sign in the same way it affects a hearing person's speech. When we give deaf kids language, it massively helps their cognitive development because it gives them a language they can use to express themselves. Deaf kids will sign gibberish the same way that hearing kids will speak gibberish.
cues.zh: 语言在很多方面是人类经验的重要组成部分，而且语言在许多重要方面与认知发展相互关联。当儿童拥有结构化的语言时，这能帮助他们理解世界。无论孩子是口头交流，还是使用手语和手势，这一点都成立。聋人中风后，其打手语的能力会受影响，就像中风会影响健听人的说话能力一样。当我们给聋童语言时，这会极大地帮助他们的认知发展，因为这给了他们一种可以用来表达自己的语言。聋童会打出手语版的“胡言乱语”，就像健听儿童会说出胡言乱语一样。

cues.en: Speaking to BBC News, professor Graham Turner of Herowitwat University said these languages use the face, body, and hands in an integrated way, exploiting their multidimensional
cues.zh: 在接受 BBC News 采访时，Herowitwat 大学的 Graham Turner 教授表示，这些语言以整合的方式运用面部、身体和双手，利用其多维

cues.en: and extremely precise visual elements. So communication in ASL or any other sign language entails acquiring command of a far more complex system of linguistic expression. I bring this up because sign language is a language in its own right, and it needs to be treated as such. Language is about the transmission of information. ASL has features that reflect the fact it's a visual language. It has a different structure, word order, and grammar to spoken English. For example, what kind of cookies do you like would be arduous to sign, so it's turned into cookie you like what kind. And there's no universal sign language either. Across the English speaking world, you have ASL in The United States and Canada, BSL in The UK, ISL in Ireland, Auslan in Australia, and NZSL
cues.zh: 且极其精确的视觉元素分层叠加。因此，用 ASL 或任何其他手语交流，都需要掌握一套复杂得多的语言表达系统。我提到这一点，是因为手语本身就是一门语言，就应被当作语言来对待。语言关乎信息传递。ASL 具有体现其视觉语言本质的特征。它的结构、词序和语法都与英语口语不同。例如，“你喜欢哪种饼干”用手语表达会很费力，所以会变成“饼干 你 喜欢 什么种类”。而且也不存在通用手语。在整个英语世界，美国和加拿大用 ASL，英国用 BSL，爱尔兰用 ISL，澳大利亚用 Auslan，新西兰用 NZSL

cues.en: The issue is that the researchers who worked with Coco and other apes for that matter didn't know sign language. According to the journalist Arden Neisser, who wrote the book The Other Side of Silence, Sign Language and the Deaf Community in America, researchers in aid communications
cues.zh: 问题在于，和 Coco 以及其他类人猿打交道的那些研究者根本不懂手语。据记者 Arden Neisser（著有《沉默的另一面：美国手语与聋人社区》）说，辅助沟通领域的研究者

cues.en: didn't treat sign language
cues.zh: 并不把手语

cues.en: as a language. Rather, researchers learned floating signs, that is to say individual words, and then just assume that they could slap English on top of it and call it a day. They imposed English oral features and English oral grammar onto ASL. For example, Patterson's papers on Coco state that Coco's two sign combinations are semantically equivalent to the two word utterances of a child. Her evidence for this is Coco using spoken word orders, agent action,
cues.zh: 当作一种语言。更确切地说，研究者学的是孤立的手势，也就是单个词，然后就以为可以把英语硬套上去，草草了事。他们把英语口语的特征和英语口语语法强加到 ASL 上。比如，Patterson 关于 Coco 的论文称，Coco 的两个手势组合在语义上等同于儿童的两个词话语。她的证据是 Coco 使用了口语词序，即施事—动作，

cues.en: ASL doesn't use spoken word orders. Another example, Coco's rhymes. In ASL, the principle of rhyming is that rhymes look similar. They have visual rhythm. So high high swing arms, cat whiskers fiddle is a rhyme in ASL because swing arms has a similar movement to fiddle. So Coco's poem, pink pink stink nice drink. Pink, stink, and drink are words that rhyme in spoken English.
cues.zh: ASL 不使用口语的词序。另一个例子是 Coco 的押韵。在 ASL 中，押韵的原则是押韵的手势看起来相似。它们有视觉节奏。所以 high high swing arms 和 cat whiskers fiddle 在 ASL 中是押韵的，因为 swing arms 和 fiddle 的动作相似。所以 Coco 的诗“pink pink stink nice drink”里，pink、stink 和 drink 在英语口语中是押韵词。

cues.en: They thought we didn't know anything about it, we were just trying to make trouble. There were three shifts in a day. I'd go in, wake up the chimp, change the diapers, and put clothes on. cues.zh: 他们以为我们对此一无所知，我们只是想捣乱。一天三班。我会进去，叫醒黑猩猩，换尿布，穿衣服。让它坐在椅子上，热牛奶，就像照顾孩子一样。我在杯子里倒了一点牛奶，然后等着它做出“喝”的手势——把拇指放到嘴边。我做出“喝”的手势，等着。

cues.en: By this time, the chimp was screaming. Even I could hear it. I wasn't supposed to give any food until he made the eat sign. I watched really carefully.
cues.zh: 这时候，黑猩猩已经在尖叫了。连我都听得见。按规定，要等它做出“吃”的手势才能给食物。我观察得非常仔细。

cues.en: She said, Nim didn't do anything with the signs. He only used them for requesting things, and even that's too anthropomorphic a description. He never used them in the deeper human sense of making a request.
cues.zh: 她说，Nim 并没有用这些符号做任何事。他只是用它们来索要东西，而即便这么说也太拟人化了。他从没有像人类那样、在更深层的意义上用符号提出请求。

cues.zh: 那完全是一种不同性质的交流。Nim 始终没能真正理解自己是在沟通。

To quote professor Graham Turner again, serious efforts to teach apes some signing began in the nineteen sixties with researchers attempting to teach individual signs derived from American sign language, ASL. cues.zh: 真正掌握手语。最多，她只是把一些关于此时此地的符号仪式化了，而且只在训练员提示后才使用。再次引用 Graham Turner 教授的话：认真教猿类手语的尝试始于 20 世纪 60 年代，研究人员试图教它们源自美国手语 ASL 的单个符号。猿类确实以这种方式学会使用一些手势。但暗示 Coco 或任何其他猿类像人类一样学会使用自然手语，是一种歪曲。尽管猿类能按顺序使用两三个符号，但对影像数据的仔细检查一再表明，训练员会提示它们，然后可疑地把各自分开的反应解读为手语句子。
